topic: A person discovers the tree they planted as a child has been cut down
text: I walk past the spot where the old oak used to stand, the ground now bare and unfamiliar. A stump is all that remains, scarred and silent. It’s not the loss of the tree itself, but what it represented—a piece of my past, rooted in this very spot. Each year it grew alongside me, a silent witness to my life’s chapters. Now, the air feels too thin, the space too vast. I circle the stump, fingers tracing the rough edges, as if by touch I can summon back the shade and the whispers of wind through leaves. The quiet here is unnerving, a sudden emptiness that makes the world seem a little less steady.
